physical_harm: Severe bleeding injuries leading to death
number_of_offences: Four accused charged, three finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimonies of eyewitnesses, including PW-6, who was in the auto-rickshaw with the deceased, and the post-mortem report indicating the cause of death as cardio-pulmonary arrest due to spinal cord injury at the atlanto occipital joint.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, finding their testimonies consistent and corroborating each other, particularly PW-6's testimony being a clinching piece of evidence.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 15.11.2001; Trial judgment: 24.02.2005; High Court decision: 21.06.2007; Supreme Court decision: 06 February 2024
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Gaurav Agrawal, D. Abhinav Rao, Ms. Prerna Robin, Rahul Jajoo, Devadipta Das, Advs. Counsel for the State: Sirajudeen, Sr. Adv., Krishna Kumar Singh, Sri Harsha Peechara, Duvvuri Subrahmanya Bhanu, Ms. Pallavi, Ms. Kriti Sinha, Akshat Kulshreshtha, Rajiv Kumar Choudhry, G.Seshagiri Rao, Gaichangpou Gangmei, Rahul Aggarwal, Amit Pratap Singh, Ms. Lothungbeni T. Lotha, Yimyanger Longkumer, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR registered (Exhibit P-32), charge sheet filed on 09.01.2002, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted under Section 302/34; High Court: Initially acquitted, then confirmed conviction; Supreme Court: Upheld conviction of A-1, A-2, and A-4; Modified conviction of A-3 to Section 304 Part II
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused 1 to 4, belonging to the same family, were involved in the murder of the deceased due to political animosity. They alleged that A-1 stopped the auto-rickshaw, dragged the deceased to A-4's house, and all four accused assaulted the deceased with various weapons, leading to his death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that A-3 did not share a common intention to commit murder. They contended that A-3 only used a stone to assault the deceased and did not participate in the initial dragging or weapon-based assault, and that the courts mechanically inferred his involvement under Section 34.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for an offence under Section 302 IPC, there must be a common intention to cause death. If the accused did not share this intention, they may be convicted under Section 304 Part II IPC instead.
precedent_relied_upon: Camilo Vaz v. State of Goa, [2000] 2 SCR 1088 : (2000) 9 SCC 1; Bawa Singh v. State of Punjab 1993 Supp (2) SCC 754; Sarup Singh v. State of Haryana (2009) 16 SCC 479; Ghana Pradhan & Ors. v. State of Orissa 1991 Supp (2) SCC 451
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the determination that A-3 did not share the common intention to commit murder, but his participation in the assault with a stone made him culpable under Section 304 Part II IPC, leading to a 10-year imprisonment.
